changes.evidence: Kraven the Hunter (2024) is set in Sony's Spider-Man Universe. Marvel Database files him as Sergei Kravinoff (Earth-688B), and its Earth-688B page gives the EarthNumber as Earth-688 ('B' only tells it apart from the comics' Earth-688). His hero twin A:sv-sergei-kravinoff already has Earth-688. It is not Earth-199999.

Spider-Man Unlimited episode 5: X-51 starts out as one of the High Evolutionary's Machine Men, the robot enforcers on Counter-Earth. He breaks his programming, and Shayne, Spider-Man and John Jameson bring him into the human rebels (Freedom Fighters). Marvel Database lists his affiliation as 'Human Rebels; formerly: Machine Men'.

Spider-Man (1994): the Insidious Six disband after their defeat (season 2 episodes 1-2, 'The Insidious Six'/'Battle of the Insidious Six'). Ock then acts alone (episode 30, Taina) before working for the Kingpin. The Kingpin brings the Six back in 'Six Forgotten Warriors' (season 5 episodes 2-6), and 'the rest of the Six disbanded once they realized that there was no profit to be made'. In the Secret Wars episodes that follow, Ock works for the Red Skull and Smythe on Battleworld, not for the Six. The group ends twice, so he belongs to no group after each ending.

Spider-Man (1994): the first Insidious Six disband after season 2 episodes 1-2, and the Chameleon is back in prison. Later he works for Richard Fisk (season 3 episodes 6-7). In 'Six Forgotten Warriors' (season 5) the Kingpin 'decided to band the Insidious Six together again and the other five members broke the Chameleon from S.H.I.E.L.D.', so he rejoins the Six. Only at the Doomsday complex does he gas his teammates and betray them to the Red Skull. The record misses the first disbanding and the rejoin before that betrayal.

owner_calls.question: Should the 1967 Spider-Man cartoon records (here A:sv-skyboy-1967, T:sv-charles-cameo-1967, T:sv-doc-ock-1967; the app uses Earth-67 for 31 records) be Earth-6799, the Marvel Database designation for the series, or stay Earth-67?
options: Keep Earth-67 (the label the Spider-Verse comics/films use for the '67 Spider-Man)
Change to Earth-6799 (Marvel Database: the reality where the 1967 animated series takes place)
owner_calls.evidence: Marvel Database's Earth-6799 page is 'the reality where the 1967 Spider-Man animated series takes place' (designation from the Official Handbook A to Z). Its Earth-67 page is 'a divergent version of Earth-6799', from Amazing Spider-Man Vol 3 #9. Jan Caldwell/Skyboy is filed as Earth-6799, but Charles Cameo has pages under both Earth-6799 and Earth-67, so the database is not consistent.

owner_calls.question: Should Spider-Ham (Earth-8311) and Spider-Man Noir (A:sv-spider-man-noir, Earth-90214) of the Spider-Verse films use Marvel Database's B designations, Earth-8311B and Earth-90214B?
options: Keep Earth-8311 / Earth-90214 (the E-numbers shown on screen in Into the Spider-Verse)
Change to Earth-8311B / Earth-90214B (Marvel Database EarthNumber)
owner_calls.evidence: Marvel Database files the film characters as Peter Porker (Earth-8311B) and Peter Parker (Earth-90214B), and gives EarthNumber 8311B and 90214B. Its notes say the film labels them E-8311 and E-90214, but they are kept apart from the comics' realities. The app already drops the B elsewhere (Earth-1610 for Miles, Earth-928 for Miguel) but keeps it for Earth-616B.
